[审稿报告]
Overall: 3.5 - Borderline Conference

# Round 7 审稿报告 — nlp_variance_gtheory

**论文**: "Reproducibility Budgets for Open-Weight LLM Evaluation: A Generalizability Theory Analysis"
**Venue**: EMNLP 2026 via ARR May 2026 cycle（deadline: 2026-05-25）
**审稿模式**: Fresh（重新审稿）
**Reviewer 编排**: 2 人参与本轮审稿（R1: 方法严谨性+实验设计; R2: 新颖性+完整性+写作质量）。Reviewer 3 为前轮 roster 遗留，本轮未分配任务、无审稿意见提交。
**日期**: 2026-05-22

---

## Summary

本文将 Generalizability Theory (G-theory) 系统应用于 LLM 评估的方差分解，设计了最多 7 facet 的 fully crossed factorial 实验，覆盖 8 个 7-9B 开源指令微调模型和 5 个 benchmarks，约 230 万条评估记录。主要发现：(1) 多 facet 设计比单条件设计需要少 10× 的 items 达到 G ≥ 0.80（55 vs 552）；(2) BF16/FP16 在 binary scoring 下功能可互换（<0.1% 交互）；(3) model×item 交互占总方差高达 36%，指示 differential item functioning。论文提供 D-study budget calculator 作为实践工具。

---

## Strengths

**S1. 首个系统性多 facet G-theory 分析 LLM 评估方差** [R1-S1, R2-S1, 共识]
同时交叉 infrastructure facets（precision, seed, temperature）和 methodology facets（prompt, ordering）与 item/model 的联合分解，在维度覆盖和交互效应分离上显著超过 Messing (2026) 的单 benchmark 5-facet 设计和 Madaan et al. (2024) 的逐因素分析。

**S2. Robustness 分析深度罕见** [R1-S2, R2-S2, 共识]
8 项独立 robustness 检查：GLMM complement（ρ = 1.0）、accuracy-range stability、Henderson I vs REML（Δ < 0.003）、probit simulation null calibration（ratio = 1.0008）、CI method comparison（bootstrap vs jackknife, ratio 0.96-1.04）、LOMO（CV ≤ 1.25%）、scoring metric sensitivity、facet specification sensitivity。在同类 NLP 论文中属最高水平。

**S3. 可操作的实践贡献** [R1-S4, R2-S3, 共识]
D-study budget projections 将方差分量转化为具体设计建议（Table 4, 7, 9），3 prompts × 3 seeds 作为最小充分设计。承诺开源 pipeline 和 calculator。

**S4. Precision separability 有即时实用价值** [R1-S3, R2-S5, 共识]
BF16/FP16 功能等价的定量确认（<0.1% 交互），直接简化评估实践中的精度选择。

**S5. 写作质量高** [R1-S6, R2 implicit, 共识]
逻辑链清晰（single-model → cross-model → cross-benchmark → D-study），G-theory 背景介绍对 NLP 读者友好。

---

## Weaknesses

### Must-Fix（影响接收决定）

**N1. [Critical] Model exchangeability 论证不充分，D-study budgets 泛化边界不清** [R1-N1 + R2-W2, 强共识]

8 个 purposively 选取的 7-9B instruction-tuned 模型作为 quasi-random facet，但论文提供的验证均为 within-sample：
- LOMO（Table 5, CV ≤ 1.25%）证明内部一致性，非外部代表性
- Forward prediction（4→8, |ΔG| = 0.035）是 within-sample interpolation，非 out-of-sample generalization
- Section 3.5 的 conservatism argument（random G < fixed G, ΔG = 0.077-0.113）表明 budgets 在方向上是 conservative，但不保证对 unseen models 的可迁移性

Model 主效应仅 2.5%（Table 2），反映 7-9B instruct 模型内的窄能力范围。标题 "Open-Weight LLM Evaluation" 和 Section 5 的通用建议超出实验支撑范围。Abstract 已加 "instruction-tuned" qualifier，但 Conclusion 和标题未限定。

**建议**：(a) 提供 out-of-sample model validation 或更充分的 sensitivity analysis; (b) Conclusion 加 scope qualifier; (c) 考虑标题是否需要限定。

**N2. [Critical] "10× fewer items" framing 隐藏总评估量 129× 增长** [R2-W1, R1 交叉 AGREE, 强共识]

Abstract 的 "55 versus 552 items" 比较中，55 items 对应 1,296 conditions/item（总评估量 71,280/model），而 single-condition 仅 552/model。Abstract 提及推荐 3×3=9 conditions 设计，但 55 items 是 full 1,296-condition 下的数字。**推荐设计（9 conditions）下达到 G ≥ 0.80 需要多少 items 这一关键数字未报告。**

LLM 评估主要成本是推理计算量，item count 为中心的 framing 与实践者核心关切错位。此问题与 N1（exchangeability）叠加——如果 D-study budgets 的可靠性本身因模型 exchangeability 存疑而打折，而实际计算成本又被低估，核心实践建议可信度进一步下降。

**建议**：(a) §4.5 增加 total evaluation budget 对比表（items × conditions = total evals）; (b) Abstract 报告推荐设计下的 item budget; (c) 使用 "total evaluation budget" 框定效率增益。

**N3. [Critical → Warning, 部分改善] Format-associated pattern 呈现层级仍与证据强度不匹配** [R1-N2, R2 交叉 AGREE, 共识]

n = 5 benchmarks 的 exhaustive permutation test resolution floor 为 p = 0.10（C(5,2) = 10 种划分），benchmark-level CI spans zero ([-1.7, 5.1], df = 3)。

**改善点**：相比前几轮，format pattern 已从 Contributions 列表中移除，Abstract 措辞已弱化。
**残余问题**：§4.3 仍占完整 section + Table 3 + Figure 3，与经严格验证的 §4.4（precision separability）获得同等呈现空间。Abstract 仍提及 "observe a format-associated pattern"。

因已不在 Contributions 中，从 critical 降级为 warning，但建议进一步调整：§4.3 标题加 "Exploratory"，Abstract 使用更谨慎措辞。

GSM8K partial-credit pilot 显示方差结构根本性改变：prompt 从 25.5% → 1.2%，G 从 0.770 → 0.553，item difficulty ranking ρ = 0.26。但 pilot 仅 1 个模型（Llama），无法估计 model-related 方差分量（binary 下 ~30%）。Conclusion 的 D-study budgets 未限定适用范围为 binary scoring——Section 3.5 末尾有此 caveat，但 Abstract/Conclusion 缺失。

**建议**：Conclusion 加 "under binary correctness scoring" 和 scope qualifier; Limitations 重点强调 metric-conditional budgets。

**W2. D-study projection invariance 假设讨论不充分** [R1-W2, R2 交叉 AGREE, 共识]

三个 invariance 威胁未充分展开：(1) item pool expansion（其他 47 个 MMLU subjects）; (2) model universe expansion（加入 1B/70B 模型）; (3) temporal drift（模型代际更替）。"Order-of-magnitude guides" 缺乏量化含义。

**建议**：§4.5 扩展 Projection assumptions 段落，量化 "order-of-magnitude" 含义（如 bootstrap CI 范围 ≈ ×1.5-3×），建议定期重估方差分量。

**W3. 200-item stratified sample 代表性验证不完整** [R1-W3, R2 交叉 AGREE（降低 severity）, 共识]

10/57 MMLU subjects，CV = 3.1% 验证 sampling variance 非 representativeness。分层抽样覆盖 4 学科领域，"order-of-magnitude" 定位部分缓解。

**建议**：报告 10 subjects vs full 57 subjects 在 accuracy/difficulty variance 上的比较。

**W4. exp-002 跨基准设计不对称性** [R1-W4, R2 交叉 AGREE, 共识]

Ordering 仅在 MMLU 操控，prompt 在 MC/FF 间语义不同（MC: 选项格式; FF: CoT elicitation strategy）。MC vs FF 方差结构差异可能部分源于设计结构差异。

**建议**：§4.3 明确讨论设计不对称性作为 confound。

MC vs FF 差异仅描述性报告，未分析 item 特征如何驱动 model×item 交互。R1 认为属 future work 但同意 §4.3 应增加机制讨论。

**建议**：§4.3 增加 1-2 段关于 FF 方差分散可能机制的讨论。

1. **Model exchangeability / narrow target universe**：LOMO + forward prediction 均为 within-sample，不足以保证 D-study budgets 的 out-of-sample 可迁移性。Abstract/Conclusion 需加 scope qualifier。

Abstract 的 "55 versus 552 items" 比较中，55 items 对应 1,296 conditions/item（总评估量 71,280/model），而 single-condition 仅 552/model。Abstract 提及推荐 3×3=9 conditions 设计，但 55 items 是 full 1,296-condition 下的数字。**推荐设计（9 conditions）下达到 G ≥ 0.80 需要多少 items 这一关键数字未报告。**

LLM 评估主要成本是推理计算量，item count 为中心的 framing 与实践者核心关切错位。此问题与 N1（exchangeability）叠加——如果 D-study budgets 的可靠性本身因模型 exchangeability 存疑而打折，而实际计算成本又被低估，核心实践建议可信度进一步下降。

**建议**：(a) §4.5 增加 total evaluation budget 对比表（items × conditions = total evals）; (b) Abstract 报告推荐设计下的 item budget; (c) 使用 "total evaluation budget" 框定效率增益。

**N3. [Critical → Warning, 部分改善] Format-associated pattern 呈现层级仍与证据强度不匹配** [R1-N2, R2 交叉 AGREE, 共识]

n = 5 benchmarks 的 exhaustive permutation test resolution floor 为 p = 0.10（C(5,2) = 10 种划分），benchmark-level CI spans zero ([-1.7, 5.1], df = 3)。

**改善点**：相比前几轮，format pattern 已从 Contributions 列表中移除，Abstract 措辞已弱化。
**残余问题**：§4.3 仍占完整 section + Table 3 + Figure 3，与经严格验证的 §4.4（precision separability）获得同等呈现空间。Abstract 仍提及 "observe a format-associated pattern"。

因已不在 Contributions 中，从 critical 降级为 warning，但建议进一步调整：§4.3 标题加 "Exploratory"，Abstract 使用更谨慎措辞。

### Should-Fix（影响评分但不一票否决）

**W1. Binary scoring limitation 影响被低估** [R1-W1 + R2-W4, 共识]

GSM8K partial-credit pilot 显示方差结构根本性改变：prompt 从 25.5% → 1.2%，G 从 0.770 → 0.553，item difficulty ranking ρ = 0.26。但 pilot 仅 1 个模型（Llama），无法估计 model-related 方差分量（binary 下 ~30%）。Conclusion 的 D-study budgets 未限定适用范围为 binary scoring——Section 3.5 末尾有此 caveat，但 Abstract/Conclusion 缺失。

**建议**：Conclusion 加 "under binary correctness scoring" 和 scope qualifier; Limitations 重点强调 metric-conditional budgets。

**W2. D-study projection invariance 假设讨论不充分** [R1-W2, R2 交叉 AGREE, 共识]

三个 invariance 威胁未充分展开：(1) item pool expansion（其他 47 个 MMLU subjects）; (2) model universe expansion（加入 1B/70B 模型）; (3) temporal drift（模型代际更替）。"Order-of-magnitude guides" 缺乏量化含义。

**建议**：§4.5 扩展 Projection assumptions 段落，量化 "order-of-magnitude" 含义（如 bootstrap CI 范围 ≈ ×1.5-3×），建议定期重估方差分量。

**W3. 200-item stratified sample 代表性验证不完整** [R1-W3, R2 交叉 AGREE（降低 severity）, 共识]

10/57 MMLU subjects，CV = 3.1% 验证 sampling variance 非 representativeness。分层抽样覆盖 4 学科领域，"order-of-magnitude" 定位部分缓解。

**建议**：报告 10 subjects vs full 57 subjects 在 accuracy/difficulty variance 上的比较。

**W4. exp-002 跨基准设计不对称性** [R1-W4, R2 交叉 AGREE, 共识]

Ordering 仅在 MMLU 操控，prompt 在 MC/FF 间语义不同（MC: 选项格式; FF: CoT elicitation strategy）。MC vs FF 方差结构差异可能部分源于设计结构差异。

**建议**：§4.3 明确讨论设计不对称性作为 confound。

**W5. 跨 benchmark 分析缺乏解释性深度** [R2-W5, R1 partially agree, 部分共识]

MC vs FF 差异仅描述性报告，未分析 item 特征如何驱动 model×item 交互。R1 认为属 future work 但同意 §4.3 应增加机制讨论。

**建议**：§4.3 增加 1-2 段关于 FF 方差分散可能机制的讨论。

---

## Reviewer Consensus [AGREE]

1. **Model exchangeability / narrow target universe**：LOMO + forward prediction 均为 within-sample，不足以保证 D-study budgets 的 out-of-sample 可迁移性。Abstract/Conclusion 需加 scope qualifier。
2. **Cost framing**："10× fewer items" 隐藏了总评估量的大幅增长，推荐设计的实际 item budget 是读者最需要的数字但未报告。
3. **Binary scoring limitation**：partial-credit pilot 显示方差结构根本性改变，budgets 的 metric-conditional 性质需在 Conclusion 中明确声明。
4. **Format pattern 呈现**：已从 Contributions 移除（改善），但 §4.3 的呈现空间仍与证据强度不匹配。
5. **Design asymmetry**：exp-002 跨 benchmark 的 facet 不对称性可能混淆 format effect。

## Reviewer Divergence [REBUT]

1. **新颖性 vs Messing (2026)**：
   - R2（W3, warning）：增量主要是"更多 facet + 更多 benchmark"，概念上是标准 G-theory 的直接扩展，新颖性有限。
   - R1（REBUT）：交叉 infrastructure + methodology 的联合分析不是 trivial extension——只有同时交叉才能发现 precision 可忽略、seed/temperature 的 item-conditional 效应。D-study calculator 作为 resource 有独立价值。对 EMNLP 这样以应用为导向的 venue，构成充分贡献。
   - **Director 判断**：R1 的反驳有理。论文的价值不在方法论创新而在首次系统应用+可操作工具。但 R2 的关切也合理——如果定位为"应用+工具"论文而非"方法创新"论文，framing 应相应调整。

---

## Questions（需作者澄清）

1. **推荐 3×3 设计在 G ≥ 0.80 时需多少 items？** 这是解决 cost framing 问题的关键数字。[R2-Q1, R1 交叉 AGREE]
2. **|ΔG| = 0.035 对应的 D-study budget 变化是多少？** 如 55 items → ? items。[R1-Q3]
3. **模型视为 fixed facet 时 G 和 budget 如何变化？** Table 6 的 ΔG = 0.077-0.113 确认 random 假设产生 conservative budgets，但需讨论绝对影响。[R1-Q2]
4. **GLMM vs Henderson I 方差分量的绝对值差异？** Appendix A 报告 <0.3pp，但对小分量（如 model = 2.5%）相对误差可达 12%。[R1-Q1]
5. **Section 4.6 G_obs = 0.71 (sub-family) 是否意味着 budgets 仅对跨架构比较有效？** [R2-Q6]

---

## Missing References

- **Gao et al. (2024)** lm-evaluation-harness — 作为 de facto 评估工具，实践建议应讨论与其默认协议的关系 [R2, R1 交叉 AGREE]
- **Cardinet, Johnson & Pini (2010)** "Applying Generalizability Theory using EduG" — G-theory 应用方法论参考 [R1 建议, 非必需]
- **Kunievsky and Evans (2025)** — 引用准确性需作者确认 [R2]

---

## External Review

外部审稿：未配置。

---

## Visual Layout Check（非评分项）

**状态**: done（2026-05-22 14:23 → 14:26, ~3 min）

| 严重性 | 位置 | 发现 |
|--------|------|------|
| Warning | Page 2 | Figure 1 axis labels/legend/tick labels 字号偏小（≤6pt），作为论文第一个视觉锚点可读性重要 |
| Warning | Page 3-4 | 连续两页纯文本（Related Work → Method 3.1），无 display item。建议将 Figure 2 从 page 5 前移 |
| Info | Page 5 | Figure 2 面积较小，仅占左栏 ~1/3 高度，可适当放大 |
| Info | Page 7 | Figure 3 堆叠柱状图建议确认灰度打印时仍可辨别（hatching pattern） |
| Info | Page 7 | Table 3 Bold 标记规范，所有表格 booktabs 风格，专业 |
| Info | Page 5-8 | Float 位置合理，无漂移 |
| Info | Page 1-14 | 未发现 margin 溢出、公式渲染错误、未解析引用 |
| Info | Page 9-10 | 参考文献格式统一 |

**总结**: 无 critical 排版问题。2 个 warning（Figure 1 字号、纯文本节奏）为可选改进。

---

## Overall Assessment

**Overall Score: 3.5 / 5 — Borderline Conference**

**EMNLP 2026 评分标准**: 3.5 = Borderline Conference（介于可被主会议接收和 Findings 之间）

**置信度**: 4/5（两位 Reviewer 均 4/5，方法论和 venue 匹配度高）

**核心判断**:

论文在实验执行层面表现出色——7 facet fully crossed design 的规模（230 万记录）、8 项 robustness 检查的深度、D-study budget calculator 的实用价值在同类工作中均属领先。G-theory 框架对 LLM 评估方差的系统性分析填补了该领域的空白。

制约评分的三个核心问题：

1. **泛化边界不清晰**（N1）：D-study budgets 是论文最核心的实践贡献，但其可靠性取决于方差分量对 unseen models 的可迁移性——当前验证均为 within-sample，target universe 限于 7-9B instruct models 但 framing 更宽泛。

- D-study budgets 建议需加 "under binary correctness scoring" 和 "for 7-9B instruction-tuned models" scope qualifiers
- "10× fewer items" 需附带 total evaluation cost context

- 建议增加：D-study budgets 的 metric-conditional 性质；推荐设计的 total computation cost

**收到上面的审稿报告后必须按以下顺序处理**:

content.content: 1	Large Language Model (LLM) evaluation results vary across reproductions, but variance sources interact, and their relative importance shifts with the benchmark format. No study has simultaneously crossed infrastructure and methodology facets in a unified factorial design across benchmarks. We apply Generalizability theory (G-theory) in a crossed design with up to seven facets across eight open-weight 7--9B parameter instruction-tuned models and five benchmarks, totaling approximately 2.3 million cross-model evaluation records. Multi-facet designs require 10$\times$ fewer items than single-condition designs to reach a generalizability coefficient of 0.80 (55 versus 552 items), with a proportional increase in per-item evaluation conditions (e.g., the recommended 3-prompt $\times$ 3-seed design evaluates each item 9 times); cross-model projections confirm the ratio exceeds 10$\times$ across all benchmarks. Under binary scoring, BF16 and FP16 numerical precisions are functionally interchangeable ($<$0.1\% interaction). Model$\times$item interaction (up to 36\%) is the second-largest component in cross-model analysis, indicating that models differ primarily in which items they find difficult. We observe a format-associated pattern in variance concentration that warrants further investigation with larger benchmark samples. We release an open-source G-theory pipeline and D-study budget calculator for evaluation design optimization.

1	\section{Experiments}
2	
3	All experiments use open-weight 7--9B parameter models evaluated with vLLM~0.9.2 on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU (96GB) with binary correctness scoring.
4	
5	\subsection{Single-Model Baseline}
6	
7	We first establish the variance structure within a single model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) on MMLU to isolate methodological facet contributions before introducing cross-model variation.
8	
9	\paragraph{Design.} The G-study crosses six facets: 200 items $\times$ 3 numerical precisions (BF16, FP16, FP32) $\times$ 6 prompt templates $\times$ 6 random seeds $\times$ 3 temperature levels (0.0, 0.3, 0.7) $\times$ 4 answer orderings, yielding 259,200 binary observations. Variance components are estimated via Henderson Method~I with bootstrap confidence intervals (1,000 resamples).
10	
11	\paragraph{Results.} Under binary scoring, item difficulty (\texttt{item\_id}) accounts for 58.4\% of total variance, with the residual term contributing 23.1\%. All main facet effects are negligible ($<$1\% each): precision 0.9\%, prompt template, temperature, seed, and ordering each $<$0.5\%. The interesting structure appears in item-conditional interactions: prompt$\times$item is the largest at 5.5\%, followed by seed$\times$item (4.7\%), precision$\times$item (3.3\%), temperature$\times$item (2.9\%), and ordering$\times$item (0.8\%). This pattern indicates that methodological choices do not shift performance uniformly across items; instead, specific items are differentially sensitive to specific facets---prompt template variation produces the largest item-conditional effect.
12	
13	The resulting generalizability coefficient is $G_\text{item} = 0.936$, indicating that 200 items under multi-facet conditions produce highly reliable rankings. A D-study projection shows $G \geq 0.80$ is achievable with as few as 55 items in this multi-facet design.
14	
15	For text-exact-match scoring (requiring verbatim string matches), the variance structure shifts dramatically: temperature dominates at 79.7\% of variance, and $G_\text{item}$ collapses to 0.007. This metric-conditional divergence motivates our exclusive use of binary correctness for the remaining analyses.
16	
17	\subsection{Cross-Model Variance}
18	
19	Extending to eight models (BF16 subset, 460,800 records), Table~\ref{tab:cross_model} shows that item difficulty drops from 58.4\% to 37.9\%, while model$\times$item interaction emerges at up to 36\%. The model main effect is 3--5\% (MC) and 9--11\% (FF), confirming that models differ primarily in \emph{which items} they find difficult rather than in overall ability level.
20	
21	\begin{table}[t]
22	\centering
23	\caption{Variance decomposition for the cross-model MMLU design (8 models, BF16, 460,800 records). Components estimated via Henderson Method~I. $G_\text{item} = 0.896$.}
24	\label{tab:cross_model}
25	\small
26	\begin{tabular}{lr}
27	\toprule
28	Component & Var.\% \\
29	\midrule
30	\textbf{item\_id} & \textbf{37.9} \\
31	\underline{model$\times$item} & \underline{30.2} \\
32	residual & 25.0 \\
33	model & 2.8 \\
34	prompt$\times$item & 2.5 \\
35	model$\times$prompt & 1.6 \\
36	all others & $<$0.1 \\
37	\bottomrule
38	\end{tabular}
39	\end{table}
40	
41	The per-model interaction magnitudes reveal meaningful asymmetry, suggesting that instruction-tuning strategies produce model-specific item difficulty profiles.
42	
43	\subsection{Exploratory: Format-Associated Variance Patterns}
44	\label{sec:format_conditional}
45	
46	We extend to five benchmarks (three MC: MMLU, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag; two FF: GSM8K, MATH) using exp-002 (8 models $\times$ BF16 $\times$ 2 temperatures $\times$ 6 prompts $\times$ 6 seeds $\times$ 4 orderings $\times$ 200 items). Table~\ref{tab:cross_benchmark} reveals a format-associated pattern. For all three MC benchmarks, item-related variance (item + model$\times$item DIF; e.g., MMLU: 37.9\% + 30.2\% = 68.1\%) concentrates at 68--72\%. HellaSwag is the sole MC case where model$\times$item slightly exceeds item (36.0\% vs.\ 34.3\%), though their sum remains in the MC range.
47	
48	Free-form benchmarks differ markedly. On GSM8K, variance distributes across item (16.9\%), model$\times$item (14.6\%), model (10.7\%), and model$\times$prompt (8.5\%); prompt main effect is 5.4\%. MATH shows an intermediate pattern: item leads at 24.0\% with model$\times$item at 17.3\%, but residual variance is substantially larger (43.9\%). Cross-benchmark LOMO analysis shows that removing any single model changes $G_\text{item}$ by at most 0.030 across all five benchmarks (Appendix~\ref{app:robustness}). The elevated FF residuals (GSM8K 39.9\%, MATH 43.9\%) likely reflect sources not captured by our facets: chain-of-thought path diversity, generation stochasticity, and answer extraction heuristics; finer-grained scoring (e.g., partial credit) may reclassify portions into interpretable components. Since scoring granularity fundamentally reshapes variance structure (binary $G = 0.936$ vs.\ text-exact-match $G = 0.007$; \S4.1), our format-associated findings are conditional on binary scoring.
49	
50	\begin{table}[t]
51	\centering
52	\caption{Format-associated variance structure across five benchmarks (exp-002, 8 models). Variance components (\%) per benchmark; MC = multiple-choice, FF = free-form. Bold = dominant non-residual component. ``Prompt'' row: for MC, reports prompt$\times$item interaction (prompt main effect $<$1\%); for FF, reports the prompt main effect (item-conditional interactions absorbed into residual due to higher generation variability).}
53	\label{tab:cross_benchmark}
54	\scriptsize
55	\begin{tabular}{l rrr rr}
56	\toprule
57	 & \multicolumn{3}{c}{MC} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{FF} \\
58	\cmidrule(lr){2-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-6}
59	 & MMLU & ARC & Hella. & GSM & MATH \\
60	\midrule
61	\textbf{item} & \textbf{37.9} & \textbf{37.9} & 34.3 & 16.9 & 24.0 \\
62	mod.$\times$item & 30.2 & 33.7 & \textbf{36.0} & 14.6 & 17.3 \\
63	model & 2.8 & 3.1 & 5.4 & 10.7 & 8.5 \\
64	prompt & 2.5 & 0.4 & 2.3 & 5.4 & 1.0 \\
65	mod.$\times$prmpt & 1.6 & 8.0 & 0.6 & 8.5 & 2.0 \\
66	residual & 25.0 & 15.4 & 21.4 & 39.9 & 43.9 \\
67	all others & $<$1.0 & 1.5 & $<$1.0 & 4.0 & 3.3 \\
68	\bottomrule
69	\end{tabular}
70	\end{table}
71	
72	The following pattern is exploratory ($n = 5$ benchmarks; permutation resolution floor $p = 0.10$). MC benchmarks concentrate item-related variance at 68--72\%, while FF benchmarks disperse it to 31--41\%, with no overlap. Unbundled, item difficulty alone accounts for 34--38\% (MC) versus 17--24\% (FF), and model$\times$item DIF for 30--36\% (MC) versus 15--17\% (FF), maintaining complete separation in both components (unbundled benchmark-level $d = 4.84$, bootstrap 95\% CI $[2.32, 8.19]$), confirming that the format gap is not an artifact of DIF bundling. The exhaustive permutation test yields $p = 0.10$, the resolution floor for $\binom{5}{3} = 10$ partitions. The item-level effect size is strong ($d = 1.73$; 95\% CI $[1.72, 1.83]$), but the benchmark-level CI spans zero ($[-1.7, 5.1]$, $df = 3$); we therefore report this as a descriptive observation with strong item-level support. This does not extend to item budgets: GSM8K requires 128 items for $G \geq 0.80$ while HellaSwag (MC, 118) exceeds both ARC (98) and MATH (101), showing that format alone does not predict evaluation cost. Figure~\ref{fig:cross_benchmark} visualizes the contrast.
73	
74	The factorial design is not fully symmetric: ordering applies only to MC (FF items lack permutable options), and prompt templates serve format-specific functions (option layout for MC, CoT elicitation for FF), potentially confounding format comparisons.
75

content.content: 1	Large Language Model (LLM) evaluation results vary across reproductions, but variance sources interact, and their relative importance shifts with the benchmark format. No study has simultaneously crossed infrastructure and methodology facets in a unified factorial design across benchmarks. We apply Generalizability theory (G-theory) in a crossed design with up to seven facets across eight open-weight 7--9B parameter instruction-tuned models and five benchmarks, totaling approximately 2.3 million cross-model evaluation records. A recommended 3-prompt $\times$ 3-seed design requires 178 items (1,602 total evaluations per model) for a generalizability coefficient $G \geq 0.80$, versus 552 items under single-condition evaluation---a 3.1$\times$ item reduction; full multi-facet designs further reduce to 55 items at 1,296 conditions per item. Cross-model projections confirm item reductions exceed 10$\times$ across all five benchmarks (for the studied 7--9B model class under binary scoring). Under binary scoring, BF16 and FP16 numerical precisions are functionally interchangeable ($<$0.1\% interaction). Model$\times$item interaction (up to 36\%) is the second-largest component in cross-model analysis, indicating that models differ primarily in which items they find difficult. We observe suggestive but statistically underpowered format-associated differences in variance concentration that warrant investigation with larger benchmark samples. We release an open-source G-theory pipeline and D-study budget calculator for evaluation design optimization.

1	\section{Experiments}
2	
3	All experiments use open-weight 7--9B parameter models evaluated with vLLM~0.9.2 on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU (96GB) with binary correctness scoring.
4	
5	\subsection{Single-Model Baseline}
6	
7	We first establish the variance structure within a single model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) on MMLU to isolate methodological facet contributions before introducing cross-model variation.
8	
9	\paragraph{Design.} The G-study crosses six facets: 200 items $\times$ 3 numerical precisions (BF16, FP16, FP32) $\times$ 6 prompt templates $\times$ 6 random seeds $\times$ 3 temperature levels (0.0, 0.3, 0.7) $\times$ 4 answer orderings, yielding 259,200 binary observations. Variance components are estimated via Henderson Method~I with bootstrap confidence intervals (1,000 resamples).
10	
11	\paragraph{Results.} Under binary scoring, item difficulty (\texttt{item\_id}) accounts for 58.4\% of total variance, with the residual term contributing 23.1\%. All main facet effects are negligible ($<$1\% each): precision 0.9\%, prompt template, temperature, seed, and ordering each $<$0.5\%. The interesting structure appears in item-conditional interactions: prompt$\times$item is the largest at 5.5\%, followed by seed$\times$item (4.7\%), precision$\times$item (3.3\%), temperature$\times$item (2.9\%), and ordering$\times$item (0.8\%). This pattern indicates that methodological choices do not shift performance uniformly across items; instead, specific items are differentially sensitive to specific facets---prompt template variation produces the largest item-conditional effect.
12	
13	The resulting generalizability coefficient is $G_\text{item} = 0.936$, indicating that 200 items under multi-facet conditions produce highly reliable rankings. A D-study projection shows $G \geq 0.80$ is achievable with as few as 55 items in this multi-facet design.
14	
15	For text-exact-match scoring (requiring verbatim string matches), the variance structure shifts dramatically: temperature dominates at 79.7\% of variance, and $G_\text{item}$ collapses to 0.007. This metric-conditional divergence motivates our exclusive use of binary correctness for the remaining analyses.
16	
17	\subsection{Cross-Model Variance}
18	
19	Extending to eight models (BF16 subset, 460,800 records), Table~\ref{tab:cross_model} shows that item difficulty drops from 58.4\% to 37.9\%, while model$\times$item interaction emerges at up to 36\%. The model main effect is 3--5\% (MC) and 9--11\% (FF), confirming that models differ primarily in \emph{which items} they find difficult rather than in overall ability level.
20	
21	\begin{table}[t]
22	\centering
23	\caption{Variance decomposition for the cross-model MMLU design (8 models, BF16, 460,800 records). Components estimated via Henderson Method~I. $G_\text{item} = 0.896$.}
24	\label{tab:cross_model}
25	\small
26	\begin{tabular}{lr}
27	\toprule
28	Component & Var.\% \\
29	\midrule
30	\textbf{item\_id} & \textbf{37.9} \\
31	\underline{model$\times$item} & \underline{30.2} \\
32	residual & 25.0 \\
33	model & 2.8 \\
34	prompt$\times$item & 2.5 \\
35	model$\times$prompt & 1.6 \\
36	all others & $<$0.1 \\
37	\bottomrule
38	\end{tabular}
39	\end{table}
40	
41	\subsection{Exploratory: Format-Associated Variance Patterns}
42	\label{sec:format_conditional}
43	
44	We extend to five benchmarks (three MC: MMLU, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag; two FF: GSM8K, MATH) using exp-002 (8 models $\times$ BF16 $\times$ 2 temperatures $\times$ 6 prompts $\times$ 6 seeds $\times$ 4 orderings $\times$ 200 items). Table~\ref{tab:cross_benchmark} reveals a format-associated pattern. For all three MC benchmarks, item-related variance (item + model$\times$item DIF; e.g., MMLU: 37.9\% + 30.2\% = 68.1\%) concentrates at 68--72\%. HellaSwag is the sole MC case where model$\times$item slightly exceeds item (36.0\% vs.\ 34.3\%), though their sum remains in the MC range.
45	
46	Free-form benchmarks differ markedly. On GSM8K, variance distributes across item (16.9\%), model$\times$item (14.6\%), model (10.7\%), and model$\times$prompt (8.5\%); prompt main effect is 5.4\%. MATH shows an intermediate pattern: item leads at 24.0\% with model$\times$item at 17.3\%, but residual variance is substantially larger (43.9\%). Cross-benchmark LOMO analysis shows that removing any single model changes $G_\text{item}$ by at most 0.030 across all five benchmarks (Appendix~\ref{app:robustness}). The elevated FF residuals (GSM8K 39.9\%, MATH 43.9\%) likely reflect sources not captured by our facets: chain-of-thought path diversity, generation stochasticity, and answer extraction heuristics; finer-grained scoring (e.g., partial credit) may reclassify portions into interpretable components. Since scoring granularity fundamentally reshapes variance structure (binary $G = 0.936$ vs.\ text-exact-match $G = 0.007$; \S4.1), our format-associated findings are conditional on binary scoring.
47	
48	\begin{table}[t]
49	\centering
50	\caption{Format-associated variance structure across five benchmarks (exp-002, 8 models). Variance components (\%) per benchmark; MC = multiple-choice, FF = free-form. Bold = dominant non-residual component. ``Prompt'' row: for MC, reports prompt$\times$item interaction (prompt main effect $<$1\%); for FF, reports the prompt main effect (item-conditional interactions absorbed into residual due to higher generation variability).}
51	\label{tab:cross_benchmark}
52	\scriptsize
53	\begin{tabular}{l rrr rr}
54	\toprule
55	 & \multicolumn{3}{c}{MC} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{FF} \\
56	\cmidrule(lr){2-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-6}
57	 & MMLU & ARC & Hella. & GSM & MATH \\
58	\midrule
59	\textbf{item} & \textbf{37.9} & \textbf{37.9} & 34.3 & 16.9 & 24.0 \\
60	mod.$\times$item & 30.2 & 33.7 & \textbf{36.0} & 14.6 & 17.3 \\
61	model & 2.8 & 3.1 & 5.4 & 10.7 & 8.5 \\
62	prompt & 2.5 & 0.4 & 2.3 & 5.4 & 1.0 \\
63	mod.$\times$prmpt & 1.6 & 8.0 & 0.6 & 8.5 & 2.0 \\
64	residual & 25.0 & 15.4 & 21.4 & 39.9 & 43.9 \\
65	all others & $<$1.0 & 1.5 & $<$1.0 & 4.0 & 3.3 \\
66	\bottomrule
67	\end{tabular}
68	\end{table}
69	
70	The following pattern is exploratory ($n = 5$ benchmarks; permutation resolution floor $p = 0.10$). MC benchmarks concentrate item-related variance at 68--72\%, while FF benchmarks disperse it to 31--41\%, with no overlap. Unbundled, item difficulty alone accounts for 34--38\% (MC) versus 17--24\% (FF), and model$\times$item DIF for 30--36\% (MC) versus 15--17\% (FF), maintaining complete separation in both components (unbundled benchmark-level $d = 4.84$, bootstrap 95\% CI $[2.32, 8.19]$), confirming that the format gap is not an artifact of DIF bundling. The exhaustive permutation test yields $p = 0.10$, the resolution floor for $\binom{5}{3} = 10$ partitions. The item-level effect size is strong ($d = 1.73$; 95\% CI $[1.72, 1.83]$), but the benchmark-level CI spans zero ($[-1.7, 5.1]$, $df = 3$); we therefore report this as a descriptive observation with strong item-level support. This does not extend to item budgets: GSM8K requires 128 items for $G \geq 0.80$ while HellaSwag (MC, 118) exceeds both ARC (98) and MATH (101), showing that format alone does not predict evaluation cost. Figure~\ref{fig:cross_benchmark} visualizes the contrast.
71	
72	The factorial design is not fully symmetric: ordering applies only to MC (FF items lack permutable options), and prompt templates serve format-specific functions (option layout for MC, CoT elicitation for FF), potentially confounding format comparisons.

   Primary objectives:
   (a) Process Round 6 Fresh Review results (3.0 Findings) → execute all fixes → submit Round 7
   (b) Process Round 7 Review results (3.5 Borderline Conference, ↑0.5) → execute all fixes → submit Round 8
   (c) Follow user instructions: "大胆干，激进一些" and "针对审稿意见快速修改" — target 4.0 Conference
   (d) Monitor 72B scale validation download (~85%, ETA ~2-3h from last check)
   (e) Manage Paper Agent, Main Agent, and Reviewer interactions for coordinated paper improvement

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Generalizability Theory (G-theory)**: Multi-facet variance decomposition from psychometrics applied to LLM evaluation
   - **D-study reproducibility budgets**: Primary contribution — recommended 3×3 design requires 178 items (1,602 total evals/model) vs 552 single-condition for G≥0.80
   - **Fixed vs Random model facet**: random-model G=0.882 < fixed-model G=0.975, ΔG=0.077-0.113, making random assumption CONSERVATIVE (budgets are upper bounds)
   - **Forward prediction 4→8 model**: MC benchmarks <3.5% error, FF ~7% error, mean |ΔG|=0.035. ARC/HellaSwag are NON-conservative (predicted > actual). FF consistently conservative.
   - **Partial-credit scoring pilot**: Binary vs step-level scoring on GSM8K — prompt effect drops 25.5%→1.2%, G drops 0.759→0.553, item rank ρ=0.26
   - **Budget sensitivity**: |ΔG|=0.035 translates to ~23% more items, within bootstrap CI range of 1.5-3×
   - **Cost framing evolution**: "10× fewer items (55 vs 552)" was misleading because 55 binds to 1,296 conditions. Now centered on recommended 3×3 design: 178 items × 9 conditions = 1,602 total evals (3.1× item reduction)
   - **Format claim nuclear removal (D023)**: After 3 rounds of failed hedging, format pattern completely removed from Contributions, demoted to §4.3 exploratory observation only
   - **LOMO 8×5**: 40 subsets across all benchmarks, all G>0.83, CV<1.3%, max|ΔG|=0.030
   - **Cohen's κ**: mean 0.326-0.461, confirms genuine DIF (not exchangeability)

   - **`docs/paper/experiments.tex`**
     - Critical: Forward prediction "all conservative" factual error fixed (line 114)
     - §4.3 title changed to "Exploratory: Format-Associated Variance Patterns"

     "Large Language Model (LLM) evaluation results vary across reproductions, but variance sources interact, and their relative importance shifts with the benchmark format. No study has simultaneously crossed infrastructure and methodology facets in a unified factorial design across benchmarks. We apply Generalizability theory (G-theory) in a crossed design with up to seven facets across eight open-weight 7--9B parameter instruction-tuned models and five benchmarks, totaling approximately 2.3 million cross-model evaluation records. A recommended 3-prompt × 3-seed design requires 178 items (1,602 total evaluations per model) for a generalizability coefficient G ≥ 0.80, versus 552 items under single-condition evaluation---a 3.1× item reduction; full multi-facet designs further reduce to 55 items at 1,296 conditions per item. Cross-model projections confirm item reductions exceed 10× across all five benchmarks (for the studied 7--9B model class under binary scoring). Under binary scoring, BF16 and FP16 numerical precisions are functionally interchangeable (<0.1% interaction). Model×item interaction (up to 36%) is the second-largest component in cross-model analysis, indicating that models differ primarily in which items they find difficult. We observe suggestive but statistically underpowered format-associated differences in variance concentration that warrant investigation with larger benchmark samples. We release an open-source G-theory pipeline and D-study budget calculator for evaluation design optimization."

We observe suggestive but underpowered format-associated differences warranting larger benchmark samples. A minimal upgrade---two prompt variants---yields the steepest per-condition reliability gain (Appendix); code, data, and a D-study calculator will be released upon publication."

     - Contribution 1 (line 19): "A recommended 3-prompt × 3-seed design requires 178 items (1,602 evaluations per model) versus 552 under single-condition evaluation for G ≥ 0.80---a 3.1× item reduction, with full multi-facet designs further reducing to 55 items."

     - Paper previously cited Δ=0.003 (from older single-subset analysis)
